public_comments.text: evening welcome good evening thank you so much for having us um thank you for giving me the chance to speak tonight my name is cindy lamb i am the president of lancaster api i'm also the co-owner of cilantro asian street kitchen you may or may not know on every corner in every block of lancaster city every road every shopping center in the county up and down route 30 every traffic line street off the beaten paths small roads to major highways there is an aapi owned business during the height of covid 19 pandemic many businesses stores shuttered so many of our asian owned businesses stayed standing not because it was easy but because we refused to give up we braved through difficult social and economic times we adapted and pushed forward because we're a resilient community but resilience doesn't mean the road has been easy even today in 2025 the the climate for small businesses, especially minority-owned businesses, has grown more challenging. Inflation, rising costs, labor shortages, and new waves of bias and xenophobia continue to test us. Our community faces obstacles that go beyond the economy, ones rooted in perception, misunderstanding, and sometimes unequal access to opportunity. We are also navigating a climate where immigrants and immigrant families, many within our AANHPI community, are often treated with suspicion, dismissed, or even targeted. In times like these, it's important to remind everyone here. Many of us, through grandparents or parents, came here out of courage. We came here to work hard and build a life, and we chose Lancaster as our home. Many of us have chosen to build businesses here, to invest in the city, to raise our families here, and share our culture with everyone. The AANHPI community has poured their hearts into building a vibrant and thriving community, and our impact can be felt in every corner of this city. We enrich the cultural fabric of Lancaster with every dish, every service, and every story that we share. By recognizing and honoring NHPI Heritage Month, you're saying that we see you, we value you, and we believe in your place here, so thank you for that. Despite living in this legal limbo for over ten years, I'm really proud to call Lancaster my home. This past year has been a journey of reflection where I asked myself if I truly fit in and if I truly belong, but Lancaster has always been shaped by immigrants and people like me are a part of that legacy. Since its founding, Lancaster has had over 250 years of welcoming immigrants and settlers, those who seek to find a better life and help build up this community and this country. Today, I find myself in fear of how people like myself are seen and what is happening to immigrants in this country.
